answers.answer: Four players select 3 Escape Pods. Place the lowest-numbered in Section A, next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. The Intruder bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults total for four players).
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 7 and 10: '3 pods for 3–4 players'; place in numerical order alternating A/B; 'All pods start with their Locked side face up'; 3 Adults plus 1 per player.

answers.answer: Remove Objective cards whose shown player count exceeds the actual count, shuffle the Corporate and Personal decks separately, and deal each player one from each deck, hidden. At the First Encounter (first Intruder miniature appearance), each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the rejected one face down without looking at others' removed cards. Eggs do not trigger the choice because they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Critical gameplay moments: first Intruder miniature triggers choosing; 'Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.'

answers.answer: Discard the Action card being played plus two additional Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2. The two Contamination cards cannot substitute for any payment. If the card has sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions from Action cards: discard that card and required additional Action cards; OR means choose one. Action Cost: Contamination cards are not Action cards and can never be discarded to pay a cost.

answers.answer: They take 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round, when they pass. Once passed, they cannot take further Actions in that Player Phase, but they may discard any number of cards when passing. They do not take damage again during later players' rounds; the rule applies at the end of their own round only.
answers.evidence: Player rounds: ending a round in a Room with Fire causes 1 Light Wound after finishing their own round; passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn.

answers.answer: On entering, flip an unexplored Room tile and reveal its Exploration token. Set the Item count by rotating the tile so the token's number faces the board's Item Counter, except no count is set for the Nest or Room Covered in Slime. Resolve the token: Silence means no Noise roll (but Slime changes Silence to Danger); Danger means no Noise roll and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the room, or places Noise in all connected corridors if none qualify; other effects include Slime, Fire, Malfunction, or a Door in the entry corridor. Then remove the token. If the room is empty, make a Noise roll unless token effect says otherwise; if occupied by any Character or Intruder, do not roll. Silence does nothing; Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders not in Combat, or fills all connected corridors without existing Noise; Slime changes Silence to Danger. The summary doesn't specify a special Noise-roll rule for an already occupied destination beyond the general no-roll rule.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll: reveal tile/token, set counter, resolve effect, and don't roll if anyone is already present.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the destination Noise roll with placing a Noise marker in a chosen connected Corridor. It is forbidden in Combat and when every corridor connected to the destination already has Noise. A Closed Door blocks player Movement across its corridor; a miniature cannot stop in a Corridor.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions: Careful Movement cost and restrictions; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors: Closed Door blocks player Movement, and no one may stop in a Corridor.

answers.answer: The provided summary does not state the sequence for rolling a corridor number that already has Noise, so that Encounter sequence and Noise removal are unsupported. It does say that a Noise marker in the Technical Corridors space counts as present at every Technical Corridors Entrance. In an Encounter, discard all Noise markers in corridors connected to the room (including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance), draw an Intruder token, and compare its number with the triggering player's hand: fewer cards than the token number causes a Surprise Attack against that player. Both Action and Contamination cards count for this comparison.
answers.evidence: Encounter steps 1–4; hand comparison explicitly counts Action AND Contamination cards. The specific pre-Encounter rule for a Noise roll onto an already marked corridor is absent.

answers.answer: Danger moves all eligible neighboring Intruders into the room, where eligible means not in Combat with any Character. If none qualify (including if all are in Combat), place Noise in every connected corridor lacking a marker. An Intruder moving into a room with a Character is not an Encounter; it simply causes Combat. Slime converts Silence to Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens, Danger; Encounters: an Intruder merely moving into a Character's Room is NOT an Encounter; Slime rule.

answers.answer: In an Encounter, a Blank causes a Noise marker to be placed in each corridor connected to that room, no miniature appears, and the Blank returns to the bag. If it was the last token in the bag, add 1 Adult token if available. In bag development, drawing a Blank adds 1 Adult token if available, then returns the Blank to the bag; the summary does not describe an Encounter in that case.
answers.evidence: Encounters, Blank token; Intruder bag development, Blank.

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in the room and simultaneously destroy the Closed Door. A destroyed Door permits movement and cannot be closed again (except by Plasma Torch). A Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Closed Door is not blocked by it.
answers.evidence: Door tokens: an Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door destroys it; several moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put. Noise roll appearance comes through regardless of a Closed Door.

answers.answer: When an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears: remove all Injury markers, return its token to the bag, and remove its miniature. A Noise marker already in the Technical Corridors space remains. Characters normally cannot use Technical Corridors, and Door tokens cannot be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors: Intruders disappear into ducts and their injuries/tokens/minis are handled as described; Noise marker is not removed; Characters cannot use them; Door tokens can never be placed there.

answers.answer: Shoot costs 1 Action card, requires a Weapon in Hand with ammo, targets an Intruder in your Room, and discards 1 Ammo before rolling. Melee costs 1 Action card, draws 1 Contamination card onto your Action discard pile, targets an Intruder in your Room, and a miss inflicts 1 Serious Wound. In Melee, a two-hit result deals only 1 Injury. The summary doesn't explicitly explain the miss penalty for Shoot, but the listed die results include a miss.
answers.evidence: Combat: Shoot and Melee procedures; Melee penalties and 2-Injury result reduction.

answers.answer: One Injury kills a Larva. Adult death is checked by drawing one Intruder Attack card and comparing its blood value to the Injury markers: blood equal to or lower than injuries means death. Queen death uses two cards and adds their blood values before comparison. A Carcass is placed for any dead Intruder except Larvae. If a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow, the Queen retreats; either of its two cards showing the symbol is enough, and it is moved through the Corridor indicated by a drawn Event card.
answers.evidence: Intruder Injuries and death; Retreat: Queen/Breeders retreat if either of their two cards shows the symbol.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the room, each targeting the escaping Character. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the room they tried to escape from. If they survive, complete movement into the neighboring room and, if it is unexplored, explore normally; if empty, make a Noise roll.
answers.evidence: Character Escape: one separate Attack per Intruder before moving; death leaves Corpse behind; survival completes move with Noise roll if destination empty and exploration normally if unexplored.

answers.answer: With several Characters in the room, target the player with the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the First Player token holder, or next player in turn order. A hit occurs when the drawn Intruder Attack card's symbol matches the attacking Intruder type. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature, put it on the target's Character board, and give the target 1 Contamination card on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards: drawn card goes on top of Action discard pile.

answers.answer: At 3 Serious Wounds, any further Wound, including a Light Wound, kills the Character; dressing a Serious Wound only ignores its effect and it still counts toward the limit. A third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound, as specified by the healing effect. On death, put a Character Corpse token in the room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death; Player Reference key numbers.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the Character's hand, removing non-Infected ones; an Infected result places a Larva on the board (with an existing Larva, death and a Creeper). Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand, and discard, removes all Infected ones, and removes a Larva if present. Surgery then causes 1 Light Wound, automatically passes the Character, and shuffles all Action cards including hand back into the deck.
answers.evidence: Room Actions: Canteen/Shower; Surgery description.

answers.answer: In a room with uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee can target them; each Injury destroys one Egg. Grenades destroy 2 Eggs and Molotov Cocktails destroy 1. A missed Melee against Eggs causes neither a Contamination card nor a Wound. After every attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll. Fire in a room with uncarried Eggs destroys 1 Egg during each Fire Damage step. The Nest is destroyed when no Eggs remain, marked with 1 Injury. The summary does not specify additional grenade/weapon targeting mechanics beyond these points.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest: destroying Eggs, Melee exception, Noise roll after each attempt, Fire damage, Nest destruction.

answers.answer: Pods start Locked and can be unlocked manually by Items or Hatch Control, or automatically on the first Character death or when Self-Destruct reaches a yellow space. Enter through the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action, first making a Noise roll; entry fails if an Intruder appears or is present, or if the room has a Malfunction marker. Each Pod holds up to 2 Characters; Heavy Objects do not use Character spaces. After entering, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round of a Player Phase, exit voluntarily for free, or automatically pass if you don't launch. If an Intruder appears in the Evacuation Section Room, all Pod occupants return to that room; another Character entering your Pod may launch it immediately.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods rules and Room Actions: Evacuation Section A/B.

answers.answer: Victory checks occur in order: Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, Objectives. Two or three Damaged Engines cause the ship to explode, killing hibernating Characters and everything else aboard. A non-Earth destination kills hibernating Characters; a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives hibernation if destination is Mars. During Contamination check, every surviving Character, whether hibernating or evacuated, checks their Contamination cards. If infected cards are found, shuffle all Action and Contamination cards and draw four; any Contamination card among those means death. A Larva skips scanning and goes directly to that draw-four check. Pod passengers do need Contamination checks.
answers.evidence: Victory Check order and rules: Coordinates exception for Quarantine/Mars; Contamination check applies to each surviving Character (hibernating or evacuated).
